text:
Lina Torres: Heads-up for the 19:00 UTC change window: we're doing a canary publish for the Python + TS SDKs (rc candidate). Need final ops + docs signoff before publish.
Ethan Zhao: I can do the publish and watch. What's the exact tag and artifacts?
Lina Torres: tag will be v2.3.0-rc3-canary. Artifacts: `redwood-sdk-python` wheel + sdist, `@redwood/sdk-ts` npm canary tag. Also want to include the small deprecation blurb about legacy sync client in the release notes.
Ravi Kumar: I'll own the release notes and docs snippet. Will push a tiny PR with the migration snippet and link to the migration script.
Lina Torres: deploy-bot, please schedule the canary at 1719811300 and post status here.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy job #deploy-860 at 1719811300 for packages: redwood-sdk-python, @redwood/sdk-ts. Canary tag: v2.3.0-rc3-canary. CI link: https://ci.internal/jobs/deploy-860 :gear:
Ethan Zhao: publish steps I'll run:
```bash
# python
make build-sdks && twine check dist/*
twine upload --repository testpypi dist/redwood_sdk_python-2.3.0rc3-py3-none-any.whl
# ts
cd packages/sdk-ts && npm publish --tag canary
```
Ravi Kumar: release notes draft: short bullets + deprecation: "Legacy sync client is deprecated; use async client. Migration script: https://git.internal/migrate-sync-to-async". Will add code example under "Migration".
Jules Park: quick QA matrix: auth/token refresh, streaming backpressure, embeddings sanity, pip/npm install pin behavior. I'll run the smoke harness: `./scripts/smoke/run_canary_checks.sh` after deploy.
Ethan Zhao: deploy-bot: kick off now.
deploy-bot: job deploy-860 started at 1719811300. step: build -> success. step: publish -> success for TS. Python upload to testpypi succeeded.
Jules Park: running smoke tests: starting auth, streaming, embeddings. Posting red flags here.
Ravi Kumar: docs PR incoming: https://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pulls/482 (adds deprecation + migration note).
Jules Park: smoke results: streaming ok, embeddings ok, but token refresh flow failing on refresh endpoint (intermittent 401). Repro on two hosts.
Lina Torres: hold propagation. Ethan please disable canary routing and yank npm tag while we triage.
Ethan Zhao: done: disabled routing rule `canary-2.3.0-rc3` in Console and removed npm tag:
`npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts canary`
deploy-bot: noted: route canary-2.3.0-rc3 disabled.
Jules Park: capture logs: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://auth.internal/refresh` shows 401 with invalid_claims on some replicas.
Ravi Kumar: adding a "Known issue" line to the release notes draft and adding mitigation: "restart auth sidecar if you see 401 after refresh".
Lina Torres: decision: rollback canary artifacts and cut rc3.1 once patch is ready. Who will cut the patched rc?
Ethan Zhao: I'll cut rc3.1 after the auth PR lands and CI passes. Expected time ~30-45m. Rollback steps I used:
- remove npm canary tag (`npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts canary`)
- yank testpypi artifact (via PyPI admin) and hold back on stable pypi
- disable canary routing in Console
- post a customer-facing note in release notes under "Canary status"
Jules Park: add to rollback checklist: revert console routes, revoke canary API keys if any, and re-run full smoke matrix after republish.
Ravi Kumar: docs PR comment: add explicit pin guidance for customers. For canary suggest `pip install redwood-sdk-python==2.3.0rc3` and `npm install @redwood/sdk-ts@canary` with an explicit warning. For GA we'll recommend exact pins.
Lina Torres: good. Also remind Support to expect a few customer pings. I'll open an internal incident if the issue shows up in prod. Ticket: REL-221 (tracking).
deploy-bot: deploy-860 finished: overall status: partial (TS canary published, python testpypi uploaded, routing disabled after smoke failures).
Ethan Zhao: cutting rc3.1 once auth fix merges. Will keep this thread updated.
Jules Park: after rc3.1 is up, run the same canary matrix and if clean we'll proceed to GA following the standard shiproom checklist. :white_check_mark:
